label: <DEL> delimiter step, stronger for longer sequences
explanation: Delimiter-step neuron: 98.5% of activation mass is on the <DEL> step (t == L), where it is active in 62% of sequences; it is essentially silent during the original phase and the copy phase (small spillover at recall_idx 1 and on the last original token of length-9 sequences). Magnitude at <DEL> grows with sequence length (active rate at the delimiter goes from about 4% for L=3-4 up to 47% of to_go=8 steps for L=9; L>=6 holds 91% of mass), and also depends on the first original token, which is the token about to be output: first tokens like y, o, i, 2, h, k, v, r give high precision (>0.85), while b, e, g, q, s, t, z, 0 rarely cross threshold unless L is large. (phase==1)&(~first_tok in {b,e,g,q,s,t,z,0} | L>=7) reaches dev F1 0.81, but the simpler length-gated delimiter predicate is recorded. Does not fire on input-token identity, digits count, or anywhere outside the delimiter step to any notable degree.

issues: The length-dependence numbers are wrong. Scored directly, the active rate at <DEL> rises from 0.24 at L=3, 0.27 at L=4, 0.34 at L=5, 0.51 at L=6 and 0.75 at L=7 to 0.90 at L=8 and 0.94 at L=9. The explanation says 'about 4% at L=3-4 to 47% at L=9', which seems to mix all steps (the by-L / to_go tables) with the delimiter-only rate.

There is a systematic class of misses. Short sequences (L<=5) at <DEL> make up about 13k of about 64k active steps on test (9.3% of activation mass), and the predicate excludes all of them. Their first tokens are mostly the favoured ones: precision is 0.65-0.78 for h, i, k, o, v, r, 2, and 0.49-0.57 for c, d, l, n. This is a structural class, not scattered noise.

There is a systematic class of false positives. Every one of the 15k test false positives sampled from misses is <DEL> with L>=6 and a first token like b, e, g, q, s, t, z, 0, f or x. Precision with L>=6 is only 0.29 for b, 0.35 for g, 0.41 for e, 0.46 for q and 0.46 for z.
The first-token claim is partly wrong. 'y' is listed as a high-precision first token, but at <DEL> it gives precision 0.02 for L<=5 and 0.70 for L>=6, so it is a below-average token.

The recorded predicate (phase==1)&(L>=6) misses the 0.8 bar on test (F1 0.785). It is labelled explained anyway on the strength of mass recall, but whether the unit crosses threshold depends as much on first_tok as on L, and the label leaves that out.
Claims that check out: 98.5% of mass is at <DEL>, the unit is near-silent elsewhere, there is small spillover at recall_idx 1 and at orig_idx 8, and it is insensitive to n_digits.
skeptic.revised_label: <DEL> delimiter step; whether it crosses threshold depends jointly on sequence length (longer is more active) and on the first original token, i.e. the first token to be output (h/i/k/o/v/r/2 fire even at short L; b/e/g/q/s/t/z/0 need L>=8)
